segments: 4. Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.

and captured the fortress in which they were imprisoned,
and they were set free.
And in the year six hundred and thirty-five of the Arabs,
at its beginning, al-Malik al-Ashraf 'Isa, son of al-'Adil, son of Ayyub, died in Damascus,
and he was about sixty years old.
For there was no limit to this man's lavishness,
and he was very fond of delicacies and luxuries.
And in this same year,
which is the year 1549 {error for 1548/9?}
1540 of the Greeks:
The Tatars again returned and came to the region of Erbil,
and plundered and destroyed.
And they reached as far as the border of Baghdad, to a place called Angabad (Zangabad,
Zangabad?), and plundered it.
Others of them reached Surramanra'i (Samarra),
and killed its people.
And the forces of Baghdad went out,
with Mujahid al-Din the Dawidar standing at their head,
and the chief commander Sharaf al-Din Iqbal the Sharabi.
And they encountered the Tatars
and put them to flight.
And since they feared lest they should return again,
they set up mangonels upon the walls of Baghdad.
And in this year also, al-Malik al-Fa'iz Ya'qub fled from his brother al-Malik al-Kamil to Baghdad,
and wished to enter the service of the Caliph.
And shortly after, that al-Malik al-Kamil, son of al-'Adil, the lord of Egypt, died,
and was buried in Damascus.
For he was an awe-inspiring and formidable man,
and he lived seventy years.
And after him arose his son al-Malik al-'Adil,
who was called by the name of his elder brother {or: ancestor},
in Egypt.
And al-Malik al-Salih, brother of al-Kamil, ruled over Syria,
and strengthened himself with the Khwarazmians,
and also added Khabur to them.
And al-Malik al-Nasir Dawud, his nephew,
who was at that time the lord of Kerak,
wished to rule,
but time did not lend him a hand.
For this man was learned and proficient in the philosophical sciences.
It is related of him
that when he used to go to Shams al-Din Khusroshahi the philosopher in Damascus to study,
he would dismount from his mount from afar,
and leave there the servants who were in his attendance,
and he would carry his book under his arm,
and enter unto the philosopher, read, and leave,
and he would not permit him to stand up for him.
And in this year, the Ismailis leaped upon Badr al-Din, the lord of Mosul,
but he was not harmed.
